name: crypto-random
algorithm: std OS CSPRNG draws: n calls, each filling one buffer of size bytes (32 bytes: the cost per call, a nonce or a key; 64 KiB: the throughput) (mk/crypto-random.mk).

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard CSPRNG (rand is not one)
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no CSPRNG API (std's hash seeding is private); getrandom and rand are crates; no crate stands in

notes: Work per step: one call that fills the buffer with CSPRNG output. Mk crypto.Random (Io.Random, std/sys: ProcessPrng from bcryptprimitives.dll on Windows, every call), Go crypto/rand.Read (outside FIPS mode crypto/internal/sysrand: ProcessPrng, every call), Zig std.Io.random (its idiomatic CSPRNG: a per-thread ChaCha DRBG in user space, seeded once from Io.randomSecure). ProcessPrng is a user-mode generator too (per-CPU AES state seeded from the kernel's CNG device, as the comment in Zig 0.17.0's Io/Threaded.zig describes it; not checked further here), so by that description no column makes a system call per draw; Zig's DRBG is its library's design and counts as such. Zig's Io.randomSecure, one IOCTL to the CNG device per draw, is the other form and not this column. Calls per second = n / median; bytes per second = n * size / median.

Checksum: n * size, the bytes drawn, the same whatever the random bytes are (CRY-8). No column can drop a draw: Mk and Go pass the buffer to an OS call (ProcessPrng), and Zig's buffer goes to page_allocator.free, an OS call, after the fills.
Written by the std-crypto lane (status/std-crypto.md). Not published: no number here is a measurement.
